correctness.rationale: Dividing by the smooth nonzero Gaussian locally and using one-variable Bezout for the Laguerre pair reduces the joint distributional Fourier kernel to its polynomial gcd. Independently recomputed all ten symbolic Sylvester resultants in a=d-1, finding common roots only at a=5 for (1,4), gcd s-6, and a=23 for (2,4), gcd s-30; zeros simple. For p finite, elliptic regularity and at least one nonzero spherical-harmonic coefficient force fixed-order Bessel radial decay r^{-(N-1)/2} with positive-density cosine oscillations, excluding p<=2N/(N-1) including logarithmic endpoint. Conversely the spherical Fourier-surface average is a nonzero bounded Helmholtz solution decaying at that order, providing all larger finite p and L-infinity. N=2d. No invalid global inverse of the Gaussian is required. The quantifiers cover all dimensions and exponent endpoints but only levels through 4.
